clue.text: Match with oddly cool interior, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the pieces are spoken aloud and the answer is the word that sounds like them

parts.note: the odd letters of cool, its first and third, followed by inside, a synonym of interior

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture is described as having a cool interior, by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks the first and third letters of 'cool', which run into INSIDE, a synonym of 'interior'; 'it's said' turns the spoken whole into the answer's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide with something is to agree or correspond with it, a synonym of match as a verb.

clue.text: Appeared on very big special appearances

parts.note: came means arrived or appeared
OS is short for outsize, a clothing size meaning very big

explanation.surface: Turning up on very large special screenings.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing label for very large sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameos are brief guest roles by famous actors, special one-off appearances in a film or show.

clue.text: Periodically witnesses test papers

indicators.note: periodically picks letters at regular intervals, here every second one of witnesses test

explanation.surface: From time to time, observers check exam papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' looks like exam scripts; it means loose sheets put into a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Insets are extra pages or leaflets inserted into a magazine or newspaper, so they are papers.

clue.text: A rifle emptied, held by criminal element

indicators.note: held by means the other pieces are kept inside the criminal's letters

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: emptied means the middle of the word is taken out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to rifle is to rob or ransack

explanation.surface: A gun, unloaded, is seized by a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is the verb meaning rob, not the gun; 'emptied' removes its middle, and 'held by' puts A plus that pair inside the criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon is a chemical element, the basis of organic compounds, so it is an example of an element.

clue.text: Analytical detective having some doubts

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police
an agnostic doubts whether God exists

explanation.surface: A sleuth who reasons analytically while harbouring doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector, a rank in the British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnostic means relating to identifying or investigating a problem, an analytical, problem-finding quality.

clue.text: Beginning to seem bothered?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word seem is its first letter

parts.note: if you bothered about something you cared

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is starting to look troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: S (the start of 'seem') plus CARED; read whole, the clue also describes the answer, since being frightened is how one starts to seem bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frightened visibly appears troubled and anxious, so scared fits the whole clue as a description.

clue.text: Scorn jailbird with time, aimless, endless

parts.note: a con is a convict, a jailbird

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an aimless life is an empty one

explanation.surface: Disdain for a convict serving pointless, never-ending time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like part of the jail picture of an endless sentence; it trims EMPTY to EMPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is the feeling of disdain for something worthless, a synonym of scorn as a noun.

clue.text: Cue rest missing centre of black

indicators.note: missing means that letter is absent from the word for rest

parts.note: the remainder is the rest of something

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word black

explanation.surface: A snooker cue rest is lost, along with the black ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cue', 'rest' and 'black' all evoke snooker, where a rest supports the cue and the black is the top-scoring ball; none has that sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or signal, which is what a reminder is.

clue.text: Unattached and tactful dropping one sweetheart

indicators.note: dropping means the letter falls further down the word, in a down clue

parts.note: discreet means tactful
the heart of sweet is E, one of its middle letters

explanation.surface: A tactful single person giving up a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving one E of DISCREET down to the end gives the homophone spelling meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, so things discrete from each other are unattached.

clue.text: Bad case of wind gripping one

indicators.note: gripping means the wind's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nasty bout of flatulence holding on to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad case of wind' reads as indigestion, but 'Bad case' is the definition, a legal trial gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistrial is a court trial rendered invalid by error, literally a legal case that has gone badly.

clue.text: A tabloid rejected accepting this compiler's hostility

indicators.note: accepting means the turned paper takes the setter's piece into its middle
rejected means the paper's name is turned back to front

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
this compiler's is the setter saying I'm, a contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A newspaper turned down the setter's work, provoking resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; turned back it gives NUS, which accepts IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is a feeling of animosity or ill will, a direct synonym of hostility.

clue.text: Retiring extrovert?

definitions.meaning: ... as in leaving office, like an ... president

explanation.surface: A puzzle: can someone shy also be an extrovert?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like shy, the opposite of extrovert; here it means stepping down from a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoing describes both an official about to leave office and a gregarious, sociable personality.

clue.text: For the audience, singer produces note

indicators.note: for the audience says it is what listeners hear that counts

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer with a high voice

explanation.surface: A performer delivers a musical note to a listening crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks musical but is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is everyday British slang for a ten-pound banknote, so it is a kind of note.

clue.text: Track access cut by account

indicators.note: cut by means the account piece splits the access word

parts.note: recourse is access to a source of help

explanation.surface: Getting into a running track is blocked by an accountant's ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a track laid out for horse racing.

clue.text: Watch part about king surrendering eastern slope

indicators.note: about means the trimmed watch part goes around the next piece
surrendering means giving up, so one letter is lost

parts.note: the escapement is the mechanism in a watch that controls its ticking
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A watch component, a king and a slope combine in a story of surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: ESCAPEMENT gives up one E (ESCAPMENT) and goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope at the edge of a plateau or ridge.

clue.text: Referee held up by crosses saved

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by says the answer sits beside, here within, the words crosses saved

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper's saves of crosses delay the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'by' as a link, but it is what signals the hidden run; in a down clue 'held up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor judges or evaluates, and a referee is someone appointed to judge, as in academic refereeing.

clue.text: Moderates fraud abuses online removing a line

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: removing means that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to troll is to abuse people on the internet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An online moderator deals with scams and abuse by deleting a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderates' suggests forum moderators, matching the online picture; here it is the verb meaning restrains.
explanation.definitionFit: To control something is to keep it in check, so controls means restrains or moderates.

clue.text: Hedonist say, gutted with sex in nude

indicators.note: gutted takes out the insides of the word say, keeping only its outer letters
in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bare means nude
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker, disappointed, has sex while naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for disappointed; it means hollowed, so SAY becomes SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a person devoted to luxury and pleasure, a synonym of hedonist.

clue.text: Small Conservative deceits concealing new plots

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: concealing means the deceits hide the next piece inside them

parts.note: lies are deceits

explanation.surface: Petty Tory lies hide fresh political schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like political scheming, matching the Tory deceits, but it means story lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The plots of novels or films are their storylines, the sequences of events in a narrative.

clue.text: Comparatively feeble joke crowning current Queen

indicators.note: crowning puts the joke on top of the others in this down clue

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
I is the symbol for electric current
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A weak joke sits atop a royal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'crowning' means the first piece sits above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Punier is the comparative of puny, meaning weaker or more feeble than another.

clue.text: Young boys losing heart for young women?

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: laddies are young boys, chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: Boys lose courage when facing girls.
explanation.walkthrough: LADDIES has seven letters, so its heart is the middle D.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies are women, and the question mark admits young ones may be girls rather than ladies.

clue.text: Depression could get you time off

definitions.meaning: a hollow or alcove in a wall or surface
a break, as when Parliament or a court adjourns

explanation.surface: Low mood might earn someone a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood; it is a dip in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Recess names both an indentation in a surface and a period when work or school is suspended.

clue.text: Former wife's describing skill returning accessories

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so the ex's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a former wife is an ex, and the possessive adds S

indicators.note: returning means the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An ex-wife's talent at bringing back fashion extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around; 'returning' turns the word for skill backwards before it is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are additional items or add-ons, which is what accessories are.

clue.text: Balance second partner without guilt occasionally

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the partner's letters go around the picked ones

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner for an evening

indicators.note: occasionally takes letters from the word guilt at intervals, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Weighing up a new partner while only occasionally feeling guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'occasionally' picks the even letters of 'guilt'.
explanation.definitionFit: To modulate is to adjust or regulate something to keep it in proportion, which is to balance it.

clue.text: Unemotional team almost holding crowd back

indicators.note: holding means the shortened team word keeps the reversed piece inside it
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: back means the word for crowd is read in reverse

parts.note: a lot is a crowd or group, as in 'that lot'

explanation.surface: An impassive team almost holds a crowd at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE loses its last letter to give SID, which holds TOL (LOT turned back).
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person shows little emotion or animation, so stolid is a synonym of impassive.

clue.text: Stuck in part if I cement craft

indicators.note: stuck in says the answer is lodged within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something glued into a component, as if part of a building job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like handiwork but means cunning trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever trickery or cunning, the sense of craft meaning guile.

clue.text: Shoots unedited film scenes

definitions.meaning: reed-like plants, whose stems are shoots
the first prints of a day's filming, viewed before editing

explanation.surface: A film crew's shoots produce footage not yet cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' looks like filming, matching the scene; it is the plant sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushes are both marsh plants with tall stems and the raw daily footage from a film shoot.

clue.text: Obsession is wrong over eating French bread

indicators.note: eating means the reversed piece takes the money inside it
over means the word for wrong is turned backwards

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
bread is slang for money, and France's money is euros

explanation.surface: Being fixated on a baguette is a moral failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French bread' is not a loaf: bread is slang for money, here EUROS, eaten by NIS (SIN turned over).
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation, a kind of neurosis in the sense of a compulsive mental disorder.
